exactAuditedStatement: For the canonical table and positive integers m, n, N=m+n, Delta_old=AbsB(m)-Abs_old(m, N) and Delta_young=AbsB(n)-Abs_young(m, N)+defA. With X=Abs_young these are equivalent to Delta_old=X-[AbsB(N)-AbsB(m)] and Delta_young=[AbsB(n)+defA]-X. The inclusion Hosted_q subset Pend_q needed for these identities is derived from the shared canonical foundation, not an additional open assumption.
hypotheses: Canonical positive-MEX/COPY table with the exact overlap ledger; d is injective and d(x)>x. Define Pend_q={x<q:d(x)>=q}; orbit roots are 0 and positive blocker labels.
Positive integers m, n avoid undefined negative arguments of A. Hosted_q subset Pend_q is proved below using the frozen-blocker partition.

No sublinear old-root or young-root flux bound is assumed or proved. Such bounds remain missing suppliers for the asymptotic C50 target. This membership lemma is distinct from the open direct-Q transport assertion also called A1.

independentDerivationAndChecks: Repeated preimages strictly decrease because d(x)>x, so every integer has unique root0or blocker. Forward orbits are strictly increasing and unbounded. For every root r<q exactly one orbit node satisfies x<q<=d(x); hence|Pend_q|=1+A(q-1). Old root class count at N is1+A(m-1), young count A(N-1)-A(m-1).

A hosted old-diagonal value<q would be a frozen blocker, impossible. Thus Hosted subset Pend. Above values>d(q)>q also lie in Pend, and hosted/above/absent partition Pend by row max and diag injectivity. So AbsB=1+A(q-1)-(2q+1-d(q))=d(q)-2q+A(q-1). This is a logical reconciliation of A1, not a new empirical premise.

Subtract the old root Pend count minus Abs_old from|H_m|=1+A(m-1)-AbsB(m). Analogously subtract|H_n| from young root count minus Abs_young; the remainder is defA=A(N-1)-A(m-1)-A(n-1)-1. Both lineage identities follow.

Abs_old+Abs_young=AbsB(N) gives X forms. Adding Delta identities gives-(1+d(N)-d(m)-d(n)). Therefore two lower flux bounds by sublinear b_old, b_young imply the Fekete defect upper bound. No reverse implication or either-sided canonical bound is proved; the source phrase "neither alone implies" is read as no implication supplied here, unless a separate counterexample is provided.
Boundary m, n>=1is explicitly added for negative A arguments. Conditions m>=n enter only the C50 uniform-asymptotic consumer, not the finite identities. No assumption that slope exists enters.
